record.context_brief: Breaking points of the positive spectrum
record.original_question: Is it consistent that ℵω is the only breaking point in the positive spectrum of strong polarized relations? More generally, can the continuum c be arbitrarily large while the only breaking points in that spectrum are exactly the cardinals of countable cofinality?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.15. Is it consistent that ℵω is the only breaking point? More generally, can c be arbitrarily large and the breaking points of the positive spectrum are just the cardinals of countable cofinality?

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source that explicitly resolves the consistency question about ℵ_ω being the unique breaking point of the positive spectrum of strong polarized relations, or the more general claim about cardinals of countable cofinality. A 2016 Fundamenta Mathematicae paper by Garti and Shelah ("Open and solved problems concerning polarized partition relations") states that some such problems were resolved, but accessible summaries do not confirm a resolution of this specific problem. Status is therefore unverified.

status_evidence.title: Open and solved problems concerning polarized partition relations
status_evidence.snippet: Garti and Shelah list some open problems concerning the polarized partition relation and solve a couple of them.
status_evidence.claim: Some problems on polarized partition relations have been resolved by Garti and Shelah, but the abstract does not specify which.

status_evidence.title: Partition Calculus and Cardinal Invariants (arXiv:1112.5772)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves consistency of the strong polarized relation simultaneously for every cardinal in an interval [ℵ_1, ℵ].
status_evidence.claim: Related consistency results on the strong polarized relation exist in the literature, but do not directly address breaking-point uniqueness at ℵ_ω.
